channels.name: Shop Owner
channels.description: The YouTube presence of Shop Owner Magazine — 'business and technical intelligence for automotive repair shop professionals'. Distinct from the hundreds of repair-technique channels (Scotty Kilmer, ChrisFix, South Main Auto) that dominate this space but teach DIY repair, not running the business.
channels.verificationMethod: Confirmed real via GaragePlug's magazine roundup, which independently describes Shop Owner Mag as focused on 'business intelligence, brand operations, and brand establishment' — an exact match to the channel's own tagline.

channels.name: AutoFix - Auto Shop Coaching
channels.description: Chris Cotton, 27+ years in the auto repair industry, 17,000+ hours of shop-coaching experience. Genuinely dedicated to shop management — profits & cash flow, KPIs, owner peer groups — not repair tutorials, and $61M+ in documented client ROI.
channels.verificationMethod: The vast majority of 'top auto mechanic YouTuber' lists are entirely DIY repair-tutorial channels. Chris Cotton and AutoFix kept surfacing across podcast platforms and LinkedIn as the real business-coaching voice in this space; fetched the channel directly to confirm the exact ID after several searches that only turned up his podcast (The Weekly Blitz) without a clean channel link.

notes: This category needed real discipline: auto repair is one of YouTube's biggest niches, but almost entirely for DIY repair technique (Scotty Kilmer alone has 6.7M subscribers) — none of that teaches running a shop as a business, so none of it was counted, matching the same standard applied to dental clinics, PR agencies, and real estate agencies elsewhere. Ratchet+Wrench (the definitive US trade magazine for auto repair shop owners) was strongly confirmed as real and on-topic, but no exact RSS feed URL could be confirmed after real effort, so left out rather than guess. On Nigeria: found only comedy/entertainment TikTok content ('Nigerian Mechanic', 'Max the Mechanic') and one genuine but non-channel story (Taiwo Abiri, a real Lagos mechanic who taught himself from YouTube and built a ₦25M/year business, per Face2Face Africa/BBC coverage) — a great story, not a channel.
